Explain in 3-4 sentences why a perpetual motion machine is physically impossible, referencing the laws of thermodynamics.

A perpetual motion machine is impossible because it would violate the first law of thermodynamics by creating energy from nothing, and the second law by operating with 100% efficiency without entropy increase. The first law states energy cannot be created or destroyed, so a machine that runs indefinitely without energy input creates energy. The second law requires that any energy conversion increases entropy, meaning some energy is always lost as waste heat. No device can circumvent these fundamental physical principles.
